findings.title: Embedded-post author color inverted instead of complemented
findings.body: The embedded topic-meta author link used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement keeps the light-theme branch at 70% and the dark branch at 30%, so both themes get the opposite mute level from the rest of this change. On the default light theme the name becomes much lighter (worse contrast); on a dark theme it stays too close to the background instead of the intended scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%). It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

findings.title: Custom message length color arguments are swapped
findings.body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new call uses 30% on the light branch and 70% on the dark branch, which is the reverse of the desktop modal (70% / 30%) and of the complement rule used everywhere else. Light themes therefore render this hint much darker than before, and dark themes lighten $secondary by 70% so the text is far less muted than the original 70% fade.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The edit replaces it with a 50%/50% pair, so the light theme loses the stronger heading color and the dark theme does not use the complementary 80% lighten of $secondary. Desktop topic-post.scss was updated correctly to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)), so mobile and desktop headings will no longer match.

findings.title: Group member name mute level changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses 50% for both the $primary and $secondary branches, so light-theme names get lighter than before and dark-theme names are not lightened by the complementary 70%. The sibling .title rule in the same block was already 50% and was converted correctly; only .name was altered.

findings.title: Mobile group member name mute level changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same regression as desktop: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Light theme contrast drops, and the dark-theme color is not the 70% lighten of $secondary that the rest of the PR uses for a 30% primary fade.

findings.title: Category badge notification color still lightens $primary
findings.body: In the same file, topic-list header, cell, excerpt, and education colors were wrapped in dark-light-choose so dark themes scale $secondary. .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still sets color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). On a dark theme $primary is already light, so this keeps pushing the badge toward white instead of a muted scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%), which is the failure this PR is fixing.
